comments.text: Geographically, there is an historic bias that the region is primarily defined by the Mississippi River only. Perhaps because French travelers focused on the river "starting" near the present US/Canada border. The Missouri, Platte and Yellowstone are the major parts delivering not just silt, but the spring floods (snow melt) that made the Delta an actual floodplain region for thousands of years. It was not until after the civil war that effective levy construction tamed the flooding and created a much larger cotton production region. To the point that up to about 1935, cotton was America's nr 1 raw export. That 60 year period saw the wealth of the delta siphoned off. All in all, the reel is a fair presentation of Mississippi's fatal economic flaw.

comments.author: @larrypanellajazzsaxophone8013
comments.text: I've been a college educator in Mississippi for just over 30 years. It amazes me the lack of vision for what could be. There is an undercurrent of trying to keep or maintain what people know rather than doing new things. That's not so much a feature of education as it is the general culture. There's a look to the left and right and if they're keeping up, they think that is good enough. It is entrenched mediocrity in many areas of life, but with a few upshots of outstanding. The first heart transplant was done in this state for example (it was not a success but gave the patient about 60-90 minutes more of life and set the stage for the first successful transplant in South Africa about 4 years later). Obviously music is something this state is famous for and we have numerous outstanding examples that way as well.  However, there is not a lot of attraction here for non-natives other than affordability, and the natives - often very family oriented, can be reluctant to go elsewhere and learn new things. A look in the local phone book and you will see long lists of the same last names and they are all related in some manner or another. I do not regret coming here, but I've had to learn how to channel lots of frustration. I'll be moving on soon but will never forget some of the many good things I experienced along with the challenges.
